title: Malware Spreads Across Isolated Government Networks via SMB and Pipes
content_md: Note: Create your free account in SOCFortress Signals ( https://signals.socfortress.co/ ) for: Global intelligence Security advisories, search & filters Microsoft Patch Tuesday & CISA KEV views Threat actor, malware & IOC views Source references, visualizations & timeline Intro A stealthy espionage campaign tracked as StingyBasilisk has been actively infiltrating segregated government environments since April 2022 by leveraging Windows named pipes and the SMB file-sharing protocol to bypass perimeter defences. The attackers utilize custom agents and malicious loaders like CunningDoor to move laterally across isolated network segments without leaving obvious artifacts on disk. To maintain long-term access across reboots, the threat actors abuse COM hijacking and manipulate the Windows Time service to execute payloads exclusively in memory. The operation relies on normal system processes to blend in with legitimate traffic, making traditional detection difficult for security teams. Analysts recommend that defenders closely monitor named pipe activity , restrict internal network protocols, and inspect registry keys for unusual modifications. First identified in threat intelligence research published by Positive Technologies, StingyBasilisk has maintained active infrastructure since at least April 2022.
